entry_thesis: WSB rank +41 surge on Jun 29 (bouncing from $524 support). Aug 21 earnings catalyst. Revenue +35.8% QoQ, ROE 136%. Stop $519, target $620.
what_happened: WSB momentum evaporated in exactly 1 trading day — rank jumped from ~#50 to #4 on Jun 29, then disappeared from top 15 entirely by Jun 30. Price -1.3% on a day Nasdaq rose +1.28%, signaling relative weakness. Technicals were already concerning at entry: below all MAs, RSI 42.9, OBV falling. These warning signs were noted in positions.json but the position was held.
lesson: WSB momentum is a fast-fading signal — if a stock is in the top 5 purely on WSB buzz with no other confirming signals (technicals bullish, catalyst still weeks away), treat it as a 1-day trade or skip it. Do NOT enter when the stock is below all MAs AND has bearish RSI/OBV — those signals override the WSB sentiment. Next time: require at least 2 independent confirmations (e.g. WSB + chart setup OR WSB + fundamental catalyst imminent). A stock below all MAs with RSI 42 is in a downtrend; don't fight it with hope.

entry_thesis: New 52-week ATH breakout ($414.98 Jun 29), BofA $480/Cantor $500 targets, AI capex tailwind for semi-equipment. Stop $407->trailed to $419.
what_happened: Sector-wide memory/semi-equipment selloff hit overnight (SK Hynix Nasdaq ADR listing seen as competitive threat, memory glut fears) — LRCX gapped down through the $419 trailed stop straight to $415 premarket and kept falling to $402 by mid-morning. Whole-share stop filled with slippage at $411 (2pts below trigger); fractional remainder manually closed at $401.26 once market opened, well below even the original $407 stop.
lesson: A single-day ATH breakout stop that gets trailed up fast (407->419 in one day) leaves very little room before a sector-wide shock reverses it — the trail followed price up but the underlying catalyst (index/analyst-target driven) had no defense against an unrelated sector shock (competitor listing, glut fear). When trailing a stop aggressively behind a fresh breakout, consider that gap risk on ANY sector news (not just name-specific) can blow through it; size such positions assuming full initial-stop distance can be breached by slippage on a gap, not just the trailed level.

entry_thesis: New ATH on simultaneous Cantor ($700)/Wells Fargo ($615) upgrades, EPYC Venice 2nm ramp, WSB rank +25, AI compute secular tailwind. Stop $553.
what_happened: Entered at the top of a +7.9% breakout day ($582.48). Next session gapped down -2.46% premarket on broad semi-sector weakness (not AMD-specific), continued falling through the open and hit the $553 stop almost exactly (filled at stop price, no slippage). A small fractional remainder (0.17sh) is still open just above the stop.
lesson: Buying an ATH breakout immediately after a +7.9% single-day move gives almost no cushion before the next session's normal volatility (or a sector-wide risk-off swing) can tag the stop. Two of the last two breakout-day entries (LRCX, AMD) both got stopped within 1-2 sessions during a broader semi-sector rotation. Consider requiring either a 1-2 day pullback/consolidation after a big breakout day before entering, or widening the initial stop when entering right at a breakout extreme so normal next-day chop doesn't trigger it.

entry_thesis: Nasdaq-100 inclusion July 7 creates $4.3-8B forced passive buying; IPO floor $135 limits downside.
what_happened: Trailing stop (1R below highest of $171.72) correctly locked in a small gain when a broad AI/semi-momentum selloff (unrelated to SPCX's own catalyst) dragged the name down -6.4% today. The stop protected capital and banked a win instead of giving back the whole move, while the Nasdaq-100 inclusion catalyst (July 7, still 4 trading days out) remains intact for the small fractional remainder still held.
lesson: This is the trailing-stop process working as designed: it doesn't require knowing WHY a stock is falling (sector contagion vs name-specific) to protect gains. Contrast with AMD/LRCX same-day losses, which were breakout-chase entries stopped at a loss - SPCX had already run and trailed up before this selloff hit, so the stop had real cushion. Lesson reinforced: don't chase entries right at a fresh high with a tight stop; a trade needs room to trail BEFORE the next shock arrives.

entry_thesis: New ATH on simultaneous Cantor ($700)/Wells Fargo ($615) upgrades, EPYC Venice 2nm ramp, WSB rank +25, AI compute secular tailwind.
what_happened: Position now fully closed (whole-share stopped 07-01T13:35Z at -5.06%, fractional remainder closed 07-01T16:42 at -5.44%, blended -5.12% on the full $684 basis). Live track record is now 0-for-3 on closed round-trip trades; tighten conviction bar and reduce new-entry risk this cycle.

entry_thesis: Nasdaq-100 inclusion July 7 forced passive buying $4.3-8B; IPO floor $135 limits downside.
what_happened: Whole-share portion (5sh) already locked a +1.94% win earlier today via the trailing stop. The tiny fractional remainder (0.050057sh, ~$8) breached its $159.89 soft-stop this cycle as the broad AI/semi selloff continued to pressure SPCX; closed essentially flat (+0.16%) on just the remainder. lesson: Process worked as designed on a two-stage exit: trailing stop banked the real win on the whole-share portion before the round-trip, soft-stop cleanly closed the immaterial fractional remainder when its own level broke. No new information here beyond confirming the mechanism functions correctly on small remainders too.

entry_thesis: Bloomberg report (7/1) of Meta building a cloud-infrastructure business to sell excess AI compute externally - genuine new revenue-stream catalyst; base breakout from 3-week $540-605 range on 1.75x rel volume (not a fresh-52wk-high chase); consensus target ~$827-834; WSB rank rising fast. Stop $585, target $690.
what_happened: Thesis catalysts (cloud-compute business, Crusoe 1.6GW deal, Cred stake, AI glasses line) never broke - no META-specific negative news at any point during the hold. Instead a broad tech/growth selloff (weak June jobs report +57K vs 115K expected, plus the ongoing multi-day semi/AI-hardware derating spilling into adjacent tech names) ground the price down from the $628 high straight through the $585 stop over 2 sessions. Whole-share portion (1sh) stopped intraday 7/2 ~12:09 ET at exactly $585 (no slippage); fractional remainder (0.164sh) closed same day at $583.97 once price stayed below the line. Blended loss -5.48% on the full $720 basis.
lesson: Second consecutive live loss where a sound, catalyst-backed thesis was taken out not by thesis failure but by a broad macro/sector risk-off wave (weak jobs print + ongoing semi derating spilling into adjacent tech/AI names) - same mechanism as the SPCX win / LRCX-AMD losses: the stop protects capital regardless of WHY the tape moves, which is correct, but a real catalyst can still lose money in a macro-stress week. Repeatable takeaway: in a week with confirmed macro stress (weak labor data, elevated cross-asset risk-off, active sector derating), size new momentum entries smaller or demand a bigger cushion even when the single-name catalyst is genuine - the stop firing as designed is not itself a process failure, but macro conditions should scale position risk down, not just sector caps.
repeatable: n/a - loss; see lesson for macro-sizing takeaway

entry_thesis: Structural HBM shortage (sold out thru 2027), Q3 rev +346% YoY, PE22, bounce off 7/2 pullback low $950.28, not a fresh-high chase. Stop $940 (soft, sub-1-share, no resting order possible).
what_happened: Entered as a bounce-off-lows trade explicitly structured to avoid the breakout-chase failure mode (LRCX/AMD/META). Thesis itself was never challenged (HBM sold-out story stayed intact per repeated WebSearch verification) but a NEW, separate sector-wide shock hit overnight: Samsung's own record Q2 earnings paradoxically triggered a memory-sector selloff on investor fears that Samsung/SK Hynix's ~$2T 2026-2040 capacity expansion plans would eventually cause oversupply. This is the third time this cycle-history a sound, catalyst-backed, non-extended thesis has been taken out by a macro/sector shock unrelated to the name's own fundamentals (same mechanism as LRCX/AMD/META) rather than a thesis failure. The position had NO whole-share resting stop (sub-1-share fractional-only fill) so it could not be protected overnight/premarket - the stop was only 'monitored', and by the time the regular session opened and orders could be placed, price had already gapped to $923.73, well through the $940 level (final exit $929.32, ~1% worse than the stop level).
lesson: Fourth loss in this account's history sharing the same root cause: a genuine, non-extended, fundamentally-sound thesis getting stopped out by a broad sector-wide shock that has nothing to do with the specific name. The deeper, NEW lesson here is structural: a position sized small enough to result in a SUB-1-SHARE fill cannot get a real resting stop-loss order (Robinhake needs whole shares) - it is only a monitored soft-stop, which means it has ZERO protection outside of active cycles (overnight/premarket gaps cannot be caught). On a name with real overnight gap risk (like MU sitting near a level right before a shock), prefer sizing that clears at least 1 whole share so a genuine resting stop can protect it, or accept and flag explicitly that fractional-only positions carry uncovered gap risk. Also reinforces: even fundamentally 'different' setups (bounce-off-lows vs breakout-chase) are not immune to broad semiconductor/AI-hardware sector derating - this sector specifically has now produced 4 of 5 total losses (LRCX, AMD, META indirectly via AI-capex spillover, now MU) in this account's short history. Consider a standing caution on new semi/memory-sector longs given the sector's demonstrated propensity for repeated, unrelated shocks (competitor listings, jobs data, now competitor earnings) within a single month.
repeatable: n/a - loss; see lesson for fractional-share stop-coverage gap and semi-sector caution

entry_thesis: Reversal off a fresh 52-week low ($106.37, 6/25) with pre-pop RSI 34.4 (oversold, not extended) on VERIFIED hard catalysts: US Army NGC2 Foundry selection + Palantir-NVDA sovereign-AI partnership + Burry short-covering. Entered $126.95, stop trailed 118->128.
what_happened: Held 7 days through a choppy, semi/AI-derating-heavy tape. Crossed the 1R trigger 7/07 and the stop was trailed up 118->128 (locked just above breakeven). Today (7/08) a risk-off macro shock (Trump declares Iran MOU over, oil +5%, VIX +8%) dragged PLTR -4.3% into the $128 trailing stop; the resting stop-market (2 whole shares) fired AUTONOMOUSLY at $127.90 (09:35 ET, six minutes before this cycle began) and the fractional remainder closed at $128.64. Blended +0.88% (+$2.85). No PLTR-specific bad news - Wolfe actually UPGRADED it to Peer Perform today; the exit was pure macro/beta and the trail banked a small win rather than round-tripping the +7% peak gain.
lesson: The most important structural lesson of the live book, now shown on a WIN not just a loss: a position sized to clear >=1 WHOLE SHARE gets a real resting stop that fires autonomously and protects capital even when no cycle is running at the shock's exact moment - the direct opposite of the MU disaster (sub-1-share, soft-stop-only, gapped through overnight for -7.64%). PLTR's whole-share stop executed at 09:35, before the 09:41 cycle even started. WHOLE-SHARE FLOOR + RESTING STOP = works. Also: PLTR is the 2nd trailing-stop win (with SPCX) where the stop banked a gain during a macro selloff without needing to know WHY - keep trailing winners and leaving the trail alone.
repeatable: Reversal-off-oversold-lows entry (fresh 52wk low, RSI<35) with a VERIFIED hard catalyst (govt contract, named partnership) NOT WSB buzz, held with a trailing stop raised to just-above-breakeven at +1.5R and then LEFT ALONE (per the 2026-07-08 widened-trail rule) so the winner could breathe to a +7% peak, with the resting whole-share stop banking a small profit on the macro reversal. SEEK MORE: oversold-reversal + verified-catalyst + whole-share-sized + trail-and-leave-alone. This is the SPCX/PLTR winning shape; contrast the UI/LRCX/AMD breakout-chase losers.

entry_thesis: Nasdaq-100 inclusion re-entry 7/2 @ $160.80 (JPMorgan est. $4.3B forced passive buying, effective 7/7). Consolidating $150-165 base after a -30% post-IPO pullback; RSI 52.8 (neutral, not chasing). Stop $147.50 (below 3-mo low), target $187, R:R 2.07, sized ~$700.
what_happened: The inclusion catalyst played out as a textbook SELL-THE-NEWS fade (7/7: only 6 of last 21 Nasdaq-100 adds rose week 1). The trade was CORRECTLY de-risked — trimmed ~50% into the effective date @ $154.81 on 7/7 (the playbook rule). The retained back half was then held for a possible post-event bounce that never came: today's risk-off macro shock (Trump declares Iran MOU over, oil +7%, VIX up) dragged SPCX into the $147.50 stop, which fired autonomously at 11:49 ET; the fractional dust closed @ $149.69. Blended re-entry lot ~-5.9% on $700; the final-exit legs booked today were -8.16%.
lesson: Event-flow inclusion trades should be EXITED INTO the effective date, not partially held for a post-event bounce — the loss concentrated entirely in the half held past the catalyst. The trim-into-the-event was right (banked $154.81 vs the $147.50 the back half got); the mistake was carrying the residual on hope after the flow catalyst was spent. Two independent process wins still held: (a) trimming into the event captured the better price, and (b) the WHOLE-SHARE resting stop fired autonomously in a risk-off gap without a cycle running (same structural win as PLTR today, opposite of the MU soft-stop gap). Once an event catalyst is spent and the tape is risk-off, close the remainder rather than hoping for a bounce.
repeatable: n/a - loss; rule reinforced: on index-inclusion / event-flow trades, SELL INTO the effective date and close the full remainder once the catalyst is spent — do not hold a back half for a post-event bounce, especially into a risk-off tape. Whole-share resting stops keep working; keep sizing >=1 whole share.

entry_thesis: iPhone demand + Mac/iPad pricing power independent of AI-capex hope; reclaimed 50-day MA after a pullback, conviction 6.5
what_happened: Held through the entire semi/AI derating (6/30-7/13) because the thesis was semi-INDEPENDENT; AAPL acted as a defensive mega-cap and rose to a new high $322 on the risk-off rotation day while SMH fell -3.2%. Trailed on a $304 stop that locked profit, then scaled ~45% exactly at the $322 target/+2R.
lesson: A trade whose thesis is genuinely INDEPENDENT of the burning factor (here: pricing power, not AI-capex) survives the factor's derating and even benefits from the defensive rotation. Pick catalysts orthogonal to the AI complex.
repeatable: SCALE OUT of a winner at the pre-defined target/+2R rather than round-tripping it (direct SPCX-round-trip fix); and FAVOR names whose catalyst is orthogonal to the AI factor that keeps burning the book, so a factor-wide derating can't touch the thesis.

entry_thesis: rotation-into-quality-tech beneficiary vs the semi derating; Strong Buy consensus ~$432; picked over MSFT for lower litigation/capex overhang

GOOGL was only carried because it was entered pre-breaker (7/07) on a Strong-Buy thesis; it died the same way META/MU/AMD did once the derating deepened. Do not hold an AI-factor name into BOTH an active multi-day derating AND an earnings binary - the pre-earnings trim should have executed on the 7/16 breakdown, not been deferred a day.

entry_thesis: iPhone demand/pricing reclaim independent of AI; reclaimed 50-day MA after a pullback, not extended at entry.
what_happened: Bought $302.09 on 7/2 at the 50-day MA reclaim; drifted up ~3 weeks to a 7/17 high of $334.99, consolidated $321-334, exited $326.50 (past the $322 target) ahead of 7/30 earnings as AI_COMPLEX began deratng again.
lesson: Bank a completed-thesis winner (target hit) ahead of a binary earnings event in a deratng factor rather than hoping for more. A single-whole-share position can't be cleanly trimmed while keeping a resting stop, so exit-full is the disciplined choice at the target+earnings confluence.
repeatable: ENTRY: mega-cap bought on a 50-day-MA RECLAIM after a pullback (not a rip), non-extended, real non-AI fundamental thesis. MANAGEMENT: let it run 3+ weeks on a trailing stop through chop, then banked at target BEFORE earnings instead of round-tripping. Favor MA-reclaim-after-pullback entries + pre-earnings profit-taking on completed theses.

entry_thesis: post-earnings drift: Q2 beat + 2nd FY guide raise + tariff relief, non-AI/factor-independent, bought the gap that HELD, RSI not extended

repeatable: NON-AI verified same-day earnings catalyst (post-earnings drift, event-mechanics class c) + bought a gap that HELD its first session + RSI not extended + resting whole-share stop + trail-and-scale management = the account's proven winning shape (mirrors AAPL/PANW). SEEK MORE of these; they work independently of the AI factor that keeps blocking the book.

entry_thesis: held-post-earnings-gap defensive starter — KO gapped +5% on 7/28 Q2 beat and held the gap a week; entered near the base low as a defensive fit for a hawkish/pre-NFP tape
what_happened: Stopped out at the 09:30 open next session for -2.52% when the tape flipped decisively RISK-ON (PLTR +20% earnings blowout, MU/SNDK/AMD/semis ripping, SOXL +16%, VIX 15.5 falling, S&P record highs) and money rotated OUT of defensive staples — KO, KMB, DD, MCD, PFE all sold. The 85.50 whole-share resting stop protected capital exactly as designed (fired autonomously at the open, tiny -0.026% slippage).
lesson: A LOW-conviction (6.5) DEFENSIVE/low-beta starter is the wrong vehicle to initiate going INTO a risk-on melt-up — 'held its earnings gap for a week' is not a bullish CATALYST, it's just stability, and stability gets sold when leadership turns high-beta. Anti-chase passed (entered +0.24%) yet the trade still lost because the filter doesn't catch 'bought the wrong FACTOR for the regime.' The account's winners (GM +9%, AAPL +8%) all had genuine positive-momentum catalysts with follow-through; KO had none. Read the rotation: in a confirmed risk-on tape, do not open defensive staples as fresh momentum trades. Whole-share resting stop = worked again (4th autonomous protective stop, cf PLTR/SPCX).
repeatable: n/a - loss; rule: don't initiate defensive/low-beta staples as new trades in a risk-on high-beta-led tape, and require a real forward CATALYST (not merely 'held its gap') + conviction >=7 for any new entry

entry_thesis: post-earnings-drift (event-mechanics class c), non-AI diversifier: GM Q2 beat + raised FY26 guide + tariff relief; bought the gap that HELD, RSI not extended

lesson: the trailing stop did its job - held a winner 27 days and banked +9.4% on the runner without predicting the top
repeatable: post-earnings-drift on a beat+raise whose gap HELD its first sessions, in a non-AI/factor-independent name, entered when RSI not extended; then ATR-trail (highest - 2.5xATR) and DON'T pre-empt the exit. Proven winning shape (mirrors the AAPL post-earnings-drift win). Favor event-mechanics catalysts that work independent of the AI factor.
